--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the exploitable opponents are: slot 2 (tolerates ~1/8 defections), slot 5 (tolerates ~1/10 with initial 2), slot 9 (tolerates exactly 2 defections), maybe slot 8 (probabilistic). Also, against always C (if in archive), we can defect always."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like policy that cooperates against always-C, defects against always-D, retaliates on defection, forgives isolated defections, and probes near the end. The trace simulates the parent and other slots against a cooperator, a defector, and a single-defection probe, and analyzes tolerance thresholds. It proposes changes: always defect on the last round, probe/exploit opponents with no observed defections, and track whether the opponent punishes defections to decide how aggressively to defect.

The trace simulates probing/defection schedules against pool opponents (TFT, always C, slot 5, slot 9, etc.) and revises toward adaptive probing: defect every 10 rounds until punished, then cooperate until the last round.

STRATEGY: Parent is a conservative TFT-like policy that cooperates against non-defectors and only probes near the end (n>=95, 25% chance). Trace simulates it against TFT, always-C, forgiving, and Grim-like opponents, then rewrites it to always defect on the last round and to probe/exploit earlier when the opponent has never punished a defection.
